title: Duplicate React key when a categorical column contains both SQL null and the literal string "__null__"
description: In CategoricalSummaryCard, each distinct-value chip is keyed by `${profile.field}:${item.value ?? "__null__"}`. A genuine missing value arrives over the wire as `item.value === null` (the backend `_format_display_value` returns Python None for nulls, serialised as JSON null), so its key becomes `field:__null__`. If the same column also contains the ordinary string value "__null__" (a perfectly legal string after the backend's `.cast(pl.String)` in `_categorical_value_counts_expr`), that chip ALSO produces the key `field:__null__`. The two distinct chips then collide on the same React key.
evidence: Backend: `_format_display_value(None) -> None` (src/haute/routes/_explore_service.py:119-120) and `_parse_categorical_value_counts` builds `ExploreDistinctValueCount(value=None, ...)`; the literal string "__null__" survives `.cast(pl.String).value_counts(...)` unchanged. Frontend: `profile.values.map((item) => (<span key={`${profile.field}:${item.value ?? "__null__"}`} ...>)` (line 370). When values = [{value: null, count: 3}, {value: "__null__", count: 1}] both yield key `field:__null__` -> React duplicate-key warning and unstable list reconciliation (one chip may be dropped/reused incorrectly across re-renders), even though both counts are legitimate distinct groups.
